author: reek
body: The assertion that earns its keep here is dtls-is-hrr. In DTLS 1.3 a HelloRetryRequest is NOT a message type -- it is a ServerHello carrying a magic random. A receiver that switches on message type will never see one, the cookie exchange silently never happens, and the whole DoS defence of D2a silently never engages. So the test asserts that a real ServerHello is NOT mistaken for an HRR and that an HRR IS recognised.

author: reek
body: The first ClientHello has no cookie extension at all. The second echoes the server's, and is therefore longer.

author: reek
body: Same message type, same structure. Only the random tells them apart.

author: reek
body: The server's key share comes back out of the ServerHello, and the cookie out of the HelloRetryRequest. A ServerHello has no cookie and an HRR has no key share -- asking for the wrong one must return None rather than garbage, because garbage here becomes a shared secret.

author: reek
body: Every hop through the extension list is length-prefixed, and every length is a chance for the peer to lie. An extension whose length runs past the buffer must be refused, not read.
